headline: Prediction tools uncover hidden microbial proteins, enzymes and disordered regions
label: Microbial Protein Structure Prediction
summary: Structure and language-model predictors now reach genome-scale microbial proteomes, exposing viral-like elements, enzymes and disordered proteins.
synthesis: The common thread is computational annotation of microbial protein sequence space, where prediction tools assign structure, function and evolutionary context to proteins that lack characterization. A structure-prediction survey of roughly 10,000 Borg archaeal extrachromosomal element proteins identifies protease, glycoconjugate and capsid candidates resembling those of giant eukaryotic viruses. CAZyLingua applies protein language models to metagenomes and classifies carbohydrate-active enzyme families, finding over 27,000 CAZymes missed by other tools. A benchmark of disorder predictors supports analysis of intrinsically disordered, fast-evolving Mycobacterium tuberculosis proteins across 540 bacteria, linking these regions to virulence and host interactions and releasing an IDR database. A separate published study examines small ORFs in enterobacteria, where de novo microproteins and noncoding regulatory roles are considered. What is new is the application of structure and language-model inference to sequences previously lacking annotation.
